newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Hong Kong diesel tight as China absorbs stocks.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong diesel tight as China absorbs stocks.

text.p: China's insatiable demand for diesel imports is spilling over into the Hong Kong barge market, where stocks are tightening sharply.
Traders said China was expected to buy large volumes of diesel at least until early February before its import requirements eased ahead of the Lunar New Year holidays, which start on February 7.
Chinese traders normally take a two-to-three-week break for the festivities.
"The majors in Hong Kong now need to replenish their stocks as China has been buying small lots of diesel," one trader said.
Traders said due to high Chinese demand, diesel barge prices in Hong Kong were assessed around $270 per tonne on a free-on-board (fob) basis, compared with $260 per tonne over a week ago.
Sellers have been indicating premiums of close to $2.00 above Singapore quotes for a 25,000-to-30,000-tonne cargo cost-and freight (c-and-f) to Hong Kong, compared with around $1.50 two weeks ago.

A major recently sold part of its 80,000-tonne shipment of diesel into Hong Kong at $1.30-per-barrel premium to Singapore spot quotes c-and-f basis. The remainder of the cargo was sold directly to China.

The lower $1.30-premium reflected the fact the sale was made from a big vessel, which saved on freight costs. Other sales by large vessels from the Mediterranean were also made around the $1.30-premium level.
Traders said China had bought around 800,000 tonnes of diesel per month in November and December and might buy as much for January.
Some traders estimated official barge sales from Hong Kong to China amounted to 300,000 to 400,000 tonnes per month over the same period.

Traders said current cargo indications to southern China remained firm around $252 per tonne, c-and-f, lower than the $263-a-tonne in early December when fob Singapore price reached a five-year high of $34.35.
They said Singapore suppliers were finding it hard to cope with the demand from China as regional demand had also picked up from Indonesia, India, Nepal and Sri Lanka.
On Thursday a Chinese bunker player bought two diesel cargoes from Singapore traders at around $32.20-$32.40 per barrel, fob Singapore, for January lifting.
